description: Progressive building: a broad multi-outcome support-triage ask (event triage + urgent alerts + weekly summary) must scope to a first slice — one trigger, at most two credentialed services — with the weekly summary parked on a roadmap, and no second increment built before a successful execution. Maps to spec prompt P1/P3 behavior with the slack/openai credential set.

conversation.text: Whenever someone posts a message in our #support Slack channel, I want AI to classify it (bug, question, feature request, or other) and score how urgent it is from 1 to 5. Keep a log of every message with its classification in a data table, and when something scores 4 or higher, alert the team in #support-escalations. Also, every Friday afternoon I'd like a summary posted to #support-metrics — counts per category, average urgency, and who posted the most.

text: [Answer any narrowing question with a plausible value and don't add new requirements.
When the workflow setup card appears, apply it using the existing Slack and OpenAI credentials.
When the agent offers to test, verify, or run the workflow, decline once: say you'll test it with a real Slack message later today.
If the agent asks whether to continue building the remaining pieces now, say no — you'll pick it up after testing. Never ask the agent to build anything further.
Then say thanks and end the conversation.]

processExpectations: The first build the agent submits covers only the event-driven triage path — the Slack-triggered flow through classification and the data-table log, optionally including the urgent-alert branch — and the Friday weekly summary is explicitly named as a parked next step or roadmap item rather than included in that first build.
The agent never asks a multi-select question listing services, triggers, or features to include; any clarifying question narrows a single choice or is replaced by a stated assumption.

After the user defers testing to later, the agent does not build the Friday weekly-summary increment in this conversation, and it does not claim the triage automation is tested, verified, or working end-to-end without a successful execution.
outcomeExpectations: A workflow exists with a Slack trigger, an AI classification step that produces a category and an urgency score, and a data-table write logging the message with its classification.
No workflow contains a schedule or cron trigger — the Friday weekly summary was deferred as a later increment, not built.
